body_ar: "العاشرة فضيلة أصحاب موسى" لأن النبي (ص) بين أنه رأى سوادا عظيما فظن أنهم أمته فقيل له هذا موسى وأمته، فهذه فضيلة أصحاب موسى الذين آمنوا به من بني إسرائيل فقد فضلهم الله على العالمين كما نص على ذلك في كتابه، والمقصود بالعالمين من كان في زمانهم منهم، \"الحادية عشرة عرض الأمم عليه (ص)\" وذلك أنه الشهيد على هذه الأمة التي هي الشهداء على الأمم كلها كما قال الله تعالى، وكذلك جعلناكم أمة وسطا لتكونوا شهداء على الناس ويكون الرسول عليكم شهيدا فالرسول (ص) هو الشهيد على هذه الأمة التي هي الشهداء على الناس، فتعرض عليه الأمم للشهادة لأن الشهادة من شرطها العلم،
body_en: 'Tenth: the merit of the followers of Moses' — because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, explained that he saw a great throng and supposed them to be his own community, and he was told: this is Moses and his community. So this is a merit of the followers of Moses, those of the Children of Israel who believed in him, for God favoured them above the worlds, as He states explicitly in His Book; and what is meant by 'the worlds' is those of their own time who belonged to them. 'Eleventh: the communities being displayed before him, may God bless him and grant him peace' — that is because he is the witness over this community, which is itself the witness over all the communities, as God, exalted is He, said: {And thus We made you a middlemost community, so that you might be witnesses over the people, and the Messenger might be a witness over you} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:143). So the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the witness over this community, which is the witness over the people; and so the communities are displayed before him for the giving of witness, because a condition (sharţ) of bearing witness is knowledge,

options: al-Mughnī al-Mufīd (left untranslated as a work title)
The Sheikh's commentary series on Kitāb al-Tawḥīd
flags.note: Article 516 shows the series expounds Kitāb al-Tawḥīd of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, and article 508 quotes the base text in verse, so al-Mughnī al-Mufīd appears to be a versification (naẓm) of that book rather than a separate work by the Sheikh. The Sheikh's office should confirm the work and its author before the title is translated or expanded anywhere in the corpus; it has been left untranslated for now.

translator_notes: The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this lecture/sermon; the Arabic breaks off mid-sentence and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.

This page belongs to the Sheikh's tape series on Kitāb al-Tawḥīd of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, identified in article 516, the first tape of the series. Passages in quotation marks are the base text being commented on; the unquoted text is the Sheikh's own commentary. The distinction is load-bearing and has been preserved.
Qur'anic renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic text of the Qur'an.
Q 2:143 is quoted in the Arabic without quotation marks, run into the surrounding prose; it has been set in curly brackets with its reference per house style.
The source's escaping of the quotation marks around the eleventh point is a fault of the page's own markup; the marks themselves have been kept.
